key_insight: Pre-trained diffusion models can be used as a non-invasive, test-time corrective supervisor for 3D Gaussian Splatting—boosting extrapolated-view fidelity without fine-tuning and thus avoiding overfitting.
problem_solved: Bridges the fidelity vs. generalization trade-off when using generative priors for novel view synthesis: removes rendering artifacts and improves extrapolated views without updating diffusion model weights.
method: Use off-the-shelf diffusion models at inference as a corrective signal for 3D Gaussian Splatting outputs (no fine-tuning of diffusion weights).
Introduce a consistency-preserving guidance/correction pipeline that injects diffusion-based priors into rendered views while maintaining 3D structure and cross-view coherence.
Adaptively apply correction strength (e.g., targeted to high-uncertainty or artifact-prone regions) to maximize fidelity gains without sacrificing generalization.
impact: Allows practitioners to improve novel-view fidelity and robustness of 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines with minimal engineering and compute overhead, avoiding the risks and costs of fine-tuning large diffusion models.
